claims.statement: PSA reported 14 operational berths on 6 August 2026.
claims.limitations: Dated operator report; do not assert a live berth count.

claims.statement: PSA’s August 2026 target is 18 berths by 2027; MPA overview states 21 Phase 1 berths by 2027.
claims.limitations: Unreconciled programme targets; show sources/dates, not a merged number.

claims.statement: The completed Tuas programme targets capacity of 65 million TEUs annually in the 2040s.
claims.limitations: Capacity is not actual throughput; 2050 is the interface horizon, not the completion date.

claims.statement: Consolidation brings PSA’s city and Pasir Panjang container operations to Tuas.
claims.limitations: Do not claim all Singapore maritime terminals close.

claims.statement: A greenfield site permits redesigned operations and industry/logistics integration.
claims.limitations: Representative model only; no as-built geometry supplied.

claims.statement: Relocating container operations progressively releases land for the Greater Southern Waterfront.

evidence.locator: Tuas Port and Changi T5, consolidation paragraph

claims.limitations: Land-use rationale, not an approved future-building model.

claims.statement: The container-terminal decision was made in 1966; Tanjong Pagar opened in 1972.

evidence.locator: Paragraphs beginning In 1966 and Tanjong Pagar

claims.limitations: 1965 precedes the decision; do not backdate it. NAS corroborates opening only.

claims.statement: Pasir Panjang Terminal’s official opening was 30 March 2000.
claims.limitations: Tuas megaport is pre-project at this era.

claims.statement: Tuas has fishing-settlement history; no dated 1958 shoreline is established in this dossier.
claims.limitations: Regional history only. NLB snippet includes obsolete port forecasts, excluded here. No exact historical village reconstruction.

claims.statement: Phase 1 reclamation was completed in November 2021.
claims.limitations: Completion of reclamation does not mean all terminal works or berths complete.

claims.statement: The first two Tuas berths began operating in December 2021; official opening followed in September 2022.
claims.limitations: Different milestones, not conflicting opening dates.

claims.statement: Phase 1 soil improvement covered 414 hectares, including 294 hectares of newly reclaimed land.
claims.limitations: Do not label 414 hectares as all newly reclaimed.

claims.statement: Phase 1 used 221 caissons for approximately 8.6 km of seawall.
claims.limitations: Not the count for Phase 2.

claims.statement: MPA describes a Phase 1 caisson as approximately 40 × 28 × 28 metres and 15,000 tonnes.
claims.limitations: Rounded envelope only; internal cells, reinforcement, mass distribution and draft not specified.

claims.statement: Caissons retain reclamation fill and form the waterfront berthing structure.
claims.limitations: Representative model only; no as-built geometry supplied.

claims.statement: Caissons were fabricated nearby, towed and submerged onto a prepared seabed foundation.
claims.limitations: No pump sequence, mooring layout, tow speed or stability calculations verified.

claims.statement: TEMAROCK combined rock placement, compaction and underwater survey for caisson foundations.
claims.limitations: Functional schematic, not a vessel replica; same publisher corroboration.

claims.statement: ARMS automated reinforcement cutting, bending and transfer.
claims.limitations: No exact bar sizes, spacing or robot design verified.

claims.statement: MPA reports geotextile pre-installation on land instead of at sea.
claims.limitations: Do not invent detailed filter joint geometry.

claims.statement: Phase 1 used sheltered caisson fabrication and dual-lane slip-form production.
claims.limitations: Show a representative fabrication process, not a verified factory layout.

claims.statement: Reused dredged and land-excavated material provided more than half of Phase 1 reclamation fill.
claims.limitations: Not all fill was sand; not a claim that any excavated material is suitable.

claims.statement: Preloading and vertical/sand drains expedited consolidation of soft fill.
claims.limitations: Drain spacing and consolidation duration remain unspecified.

claims.statement: The Phase 1 study describes settlement beacons, extensometers and pore-pressure instruments.
claims.limitations: Construction monitoring evidence, not a verified permanent maintenance schedule.

claims.statement: Ground treatment addressed demanding stability requirements for automated vehicle operation.
claims.limitations: The paper reports a 40 mm / 60-year design requirement (printed p162); retain in evidence notes only, not a universal operational tolerance or simulated result.

claims.statement: MPA chose finger-pier geometry to use land/sea space efficiently and accommodate different ship lengths.
claims.limitations: Use a clearly illustrative finger-pier district, not traced official boundaries.

claims.statement: The Phase 1 platform was built five metres above mean sea level.
claims.limitations: Height datum is MSL; not five metres above every tide or a guaranteed flood threshold.

claims.statement: An EIA and environmental monitoring programme accompanied the reclamation.
claims.limitations: Do not equate mitigation with zero ecological impact or invent compliance readings.

claims.statement: MPA reports relocating 2,300 coral colonies from Sultan Shoal before works began.
claims.limitations: Do not infer survival rates; relocation is not proof of complete ecosystem replacement.

claims.statement: The 2019 Phase 2 plan specifies 387 hectares and 227 caissons.
claims.limitations: Keep separate from Phase 1 figures.

claims.statement: Phase 2 was described as an 8.6 km wharf in 2019; the overview describes 9.1 km seawall.
claims.limitations: Different measures or revisions; unresolved. Do not silently substitute.

claims.statement: Phase 2 announced slip-form jack monitoring, modular reinforcement and automated curing.
claims.limitations: Announced method, not proof every component was built identically.

claims.statement: Phase 2 planning describes dredging, reclaimer equipment and reuse of fill above sea level.

evidence.locator: PDF p2, foundation/dredging and material-handling paragraphs

claims.limitations: No exact dredger configuration, cycle times or executed contract programme verified.

claims.statement: A separate PSA tender covered Phase 2 berths and stacking yards in 2025.

evidence.locator: Tender title, ref 2025/QS/BC/PSAC/4018099 and closing date

claims.limitations: Public notice only; drawings require supplier access and were not retrieved.

claims.statement: Electric AGVs connect quay and yard; automated yard equipment is remotely managed.

evidence.locator: Deploying AI and Automation in Port Operations

claims.limitations: No real dispatch algorithm, collision controls or live operational simulation.

claims.statement: Net-zero emissions by 2050 is a stated aim, not current achieved status.
claims.limitations: Avoid invented emissions savings or guaranteed future operation.

claims.statement: The planned Supply Chain Hub includes cargo consolidation and distribution functions.

evidence.locator: Keppel Distripark / Supply Chain Hub paragraphs

claims.limitations: Keep logistics ecosystem schematic; do not infer a built 2026 layout.

claims.statement: Proposed cutaways and animated placement/drainage explain relationships rather than calculate real performance.
claims.limitations: All camera layouts, particles, component spacing and timings are original schematic choices.

claims.statement: The Phase 1 paper describes local soft-ground replacement with compacted sand beneath quay foundations.
claims.limitations: Where required, with varying depth; do not depict one uniform sand key under the whole port.
